objective: Stop the remote gate from compiling the Rust dependency graph twice, bound a slow or stuck run, and remove the two stale workflows that would fail on a tag.
changes: scripts/verify runs cargo test --release --locked and then cargo build --release --locked in one target directory; the debug cargo check/test pair is gone
ci.yml caches ~/.cargo, Calix.Ui.Gpui/target and ~/.cache/zig, keyed by Cargo.lock and the Zig manifests
ci.yml gives Verify a 35-minute step timeout and the job a 45-minute timeout
.github/workflows/release.yml and build-and-publish.yml are deleted; ci.yml is the only workflow and owns tag builds and GitHub releases
docs/ci.md records the single-profile build, the cache, the timeouts and the workflow ownership

remote_run.finding: Not a loop. The log shows the steps running once, in order. At cancellation the job was in the final rust-release-build step; it had been there 731 seconds. The prior green run 39398808673 spent 864 seconds in that same step and 1826 seconds in Verify, so the duration was cold-compile cost, not a retry cycle.
remote_run.cost_note: The cancellation completed. No further remote run was dispatched for this change.

local.note: The host shares a warm Cargo target; the timings show correctness, not a cold build.

container_baseline.note: Baseline before this change: debug check/test plus a separate release build.

container_after.note: The release test compile and the release binary build share one target directory. The local saving is small because this host has a warm shared cache; the remote saving is the removed debug compile.

worktree_rehearsal.commit: uncommitted worktree at e05bda75 plus the staged change

known_gaps: The actions/cache restore-and-save path is GitHub-hosted behavior. The cached paths exist after the local container build, but a cache hit could not be exercised locally. The first tag run remains cold and must fit the 35-minute Verify timeout.
The remote runner is slower than this host; the container replay proves the gate's shape and counts, not the remote wall-clock time.
